program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const g = 9.8; const v0 = inputs.launchSpeed; const t = time; const v = v0 - g * t; const y = v0 * t - 0.5 * g * t * t; const maxH = (v0 * v0) / (2 * g); const scaleY = 220 / Math.max(maxH, 1.3); const baseY = 320; const ballY = baseY - y * scaleY; const ballX = 320; let motionState = "Moving up"; if (Math.abs(v) < 0.05) { motionState = "Still for an instant"; } else if (v < 0) { motionState = "Moving down"; } const gravityState = "Gravity pulls down"; const objects = []; objects.push(sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 340, title: "Vertical Throw", state: motionState })); objects.push(sdk.axis("axis.height", { x: 120, y: 320, length: 260, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: Math.max(maxH * 1.2, 1.5), label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.groundMark("ground.launchL", ballX - 30, baseY + 12, 60, "Launch")); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, ballY, 28, { role: "output" })); objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 22, y: ballY }, { value: Math.abs(v) < 0.05 ? 0 : v, direction: "up" }, { scale: 12, minLength: 12, label: "v" })); objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 22, y: ballY }, { value: -g, direction: "up" }, { scale: 6, minLength: 12, label: "a" })); let calloutY = ballY - 40; if (calloutY < 75) calloutY = 75; objects.push(sdk.callout(ballX + 45, calloutY, [motionState, gravityState], { id: "callout.toss" })); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionState }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityState }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed: v0, gravity: g, apexTime: v0 / g, apexHeight: maxH, velocity: v, height: Math.max(0, y) } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity still pulls downward.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a ball tossed upward. A blue motion arrow shortens on the way up, disappears at the top, and points downward on the way down, while a dashed gravity arrow remains constantly directed downward.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows.
